summary: 1935 CCC-built Lake County lookout burned in the 2018 Ranch Fire, then rebuilt on a 35-foot steel tower and staffed again in 2026.

facts.design: Civilian Conservation Corps lookout built from USFS plans; the Forest Service describes a 10-by-10-foot cabin on a 35-foot steel tower

access.note: Staffed Forest Service lookout on High Glade Road; the 2024 release asked visitors to avoid the road during construction. Current visiting rules are not in the sources read.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mendocino National Forest

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps from USFS plans; standard 14x14 cab per the Register
Lookout-fireman Delmar O. Tilley stationed at High Glade; accepted for military service
Wildfire overran the lookout station; station had been evacuated beforehand
Registered March 20, 2016 as US 1123, CA 109; nominated by Bill Ulmer
Ranch Fire in July 2018; the Register says the cab was destroyed about July 31 and the steel tower remains, while the 2026 Forest Service feature says the tower burned to the ground
Disaster supplemental funding secured for the design and rebuild
Forest Service release of October 11, 2024: contractors beginning reconstruction; construction site to be closed to the public
Forest Service says the lookout was rebuilt in 2025
Seasonal shift begun by two lookouts, one a long-time lookout who had served at High Glade before

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 1935. The Forest Service calls the old tower 85 years old in 2018, which would point to about 1933; this record keeps the Register's 1935 and notes the difference.

notes_for_editor: Source conflicts: cab size (Register 14x14 vs Forest Service 10x10); whether the steel tower survived the 2018 Ranch Fire (Register: remains; 2026 Forest Service feature: burned to the ground). Record 'rebuilt 2026' (FFLA 'New 2026', not re-read) vs Forest Service 'rebuilt in 2025' and back in service 2026; event dated 2025 here with 2026 staffing. Built year: Register 1935 vs 85-year-old tower in 2018. Lake County News 2026 article returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Access 'restricted' is a judgment from staffed status, not a stated rule. No photos proposed (Forest Service photo credits exist but no image URLs were read).
